book: Nancy Caroline · Chapter 13 · Airway Management and Ventilation
title: Supraglottic Airways, RSI, Failed Airways and Special Patients

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already open airways, ventilate with a BVM and suction. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Know the SGAs, and BC's line about PCPs in cardiac arrest
  2. Support drug-assisted intubation and a failed airway
  3. Ventilate special patients: stomas, dentures, facial trauma

Textbook: Chapter 13, PDF pages 1158–1264
slides.say: Welcome to the last lesson of Chapter thirteen. Last time you set up an intubation as the assistant. Today we finish the chapter with three things. First, supraglottic airways, or SGAs: devices that sit above the vocal cords, which the BC guideline mentions for PCPs in cardiac arrest. Second, drug-assisted intubation and the failed airway. The drugs and the surgical airway belong to your advanced partner, but keeping the patient oxygenated through it all is your job. Third, special patients: people who breathe through an opening in the neck, patients with dentures, and patients with serious facial injuries.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来到第十三章最后一课。上节课你以助手身份为插管做好了准备。今天讲完本章，共三件事。第一，声门上气道（SGA）：位于声带上方的装置，BC 指南在心跳骤停部分提到了 PCP 使用它。第二，药物辅助插管和插管失败的气道：药物和外科气道属于你的高级搭档，但全程让病人保持氧合是你的工作。第三，特殊病人：经颈部开口呼吸的人、戴假牙的病人，以及面部严重受伤的病人。

slides.title: What is a supraglottic airway?
slides.body:
Sits above the glottis; goes in blind

  • No laryngoscope, no mask seal to hold
  • Quicker and easier to learn than intubation
  • Tip usually rests in the top of the esophagus
  • Only for patients with no gag reflex
  • Does not fully protect against aspiration
slides.say: A supraglottic airway is a tube with a cuff or seal that sits above the glottis, the opening between the vocal cords. It goes in blind, without a laryngoscope, so it's quicker and easier to learn than intubation. Once it's in, you no longer have to hold a mask seal, which frees your hands and steadies ventilation. The tip usually rests in the top of the esophagus, and the seal sits around the opening of the larynx. Two limits matter. It's only for deeply unresponsive patients with no gag reflex, or they'll gag and vomit. And it does not fully protect the lungs from aspiration, so keep suction close.
slides.sayZh: 声门上气道是一根带套囊或密封罩的管子，位于声门（声带之间的开口）上方。它是盲插的，不用喉镜，所以比气管插管更快、更容易学。放好以后就不用再一直按着面罩密封，你的手腾出来了，通气也更稳定。它的尖端通常落在食管上端，密封部分围住喉的开口。有两个限制很重要：只能用于深度无反应、没有呕吐反射的病人，否则会引起干呕和呕吐；它也不能完全防止误吸，所以吸引器要放在手边。

slides.title: Four devices in the textbook
slides.body:
DeviceKey features
King LTOne lumen; one valve, two cuffs; LTS-D: gastric port
LMAInflatable mask over larynx; rises 1–2 cm on inflation
i-gelGel cuff, no inflation; bite block; gastric channel
CombitubeTwo lumens; ventilate blue first, then clear; age 16+

Your service will carry one or two of these: learn yours well.
slides.say: The textbook describes four devices. The King LT is a single tube with two cuffs, one sealing the esophagus and one the throat, both filled through one valve; the common LTS-D model also has a channel for a gastric tube. The laryngeal mask airway, or LMA, has an inflatable mask that covers the larynx and rises one to two centimetres as it inflates. The i-gel has a soft gel cuff that needs no inflation, a built-in bite block and a gastric channel. The Combitube has two tubes: ventilate through the blue one first, and if the chest doesn't rise, switch to the clear one.
slides.sayZh: 教材介绍了四种装置。King LT 是一根单腔管，带两个套囊，一个封住食管、一个封住咽部，通过同一个阀门一起充气；常用的 LTS-D 型还有一个可通胃管的通道。喉罩（LMA）有一个可充气的罩子盖住喉部，充气时会自己往外退一到两厘米。i-gel 是不需充气的软凝胶罩，自带牙垫和胃管通道。Combitube 有两根管：先经蓝色管通气，如果胸廓不起伏，就换透明管。

slides.title: Inserting and checking an SGA
slides.body:
1. Preoxygenate with BVM and 100% O₂
  2. Size by weight or height; test, then empty the cuff; lubricate
  3. Slide in gently along the palate; never force it
  4. Inflate if it has a cuff; start ventilating
  5. Confirm: chest rise, lungs and stomach, waveform ETCO₂; secure

Not with a gag reflex. King LT: not with esophageal disease or a swallowed caustic.
slides.say: The steps are similar for every SGA. Preoxygenate with the BVM and one hundred percent oxygen. Choose the size by the patient's weight or height, test the cuff, empty it, and lubricate. Slide the device gently along the hard palate to the correct depth; never force it. Inflate the cuff if there is one, and start ventilating. Then confirm it just like a tube: chest rise, breath sounds over both lungs and silence over the stomach, and waveform capnography. Secure it and reconfirm after every move. If a King LT is hard to ventilate, the cuff may be pushing the epiglottis down; pull back gently, without deflating, until it gets easier.
slides.sayZh: 每种声门上气道的步骤都差不多。先用球囊面罩和百分之百氧气预充氧。按病人的体重或身高选型号，测试套囊后把气抽干净，再润滑。顺着硬腭轻轻滑入到正确深度，绝不能硬推。有套囊就充气，然后开始通气。接着像确认气管导管一样确认：胸廓起伏、双肺有呼吸音而上腹安静、波形二氧化碳监测。固定好，每次搬动后重新确认。如果 King LT 通气困难，可能是套囊把会厌压下去了：不放气，轻轻往外退，直到通气变顺。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: SGA in cardiac arrest
slides.body:
BC Adult CPR/AED and CPR basic concepts

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • CPR 30:2; 100–120/min, 5–6 cm deep
  • Pauses in compressions under 5 seconds
  • AED as soon as possible
  • Avoid hyperventilation

PCP adds

  • SGA insertion by PCPs, once high-quality CPR is under way
slides.say: Here's where BC comes in. In the BC CPR guidelines, every licence level does the same core work for an adult in cardiac arrest: thirty compressions to two breaths, one hundred to one hundred twenty a minute, five to six centimetres deep, pauses under five seconds, the AED as soon as possible, and no hyperventilation. The right column has one item. The BC guideline mentions supraglottic airway insertion by PCPs once high-quality cardiac arrest care is under way. Notice the order: good compressions and good BVM come first, and the SGA comes after. That fits the book's warning from last lesson: an advanced airway never replaces the basics.
slides.sayZh: 这里看 BC 的规定。在 BC 的 CPR 指南里，所有执照级别对成人心跳骤停做的核心工作都一样：按压与通气三十比二，每分钟一百到一百二十次，深度五到六厘米，中断不超过五秒，尽快用 AED，避免过度通气。右栏只有一项：BC 指南提到，在高质量的心跳骤停处理开始之后，由 PCP 置入声门上气道。注意顺序：先有好的按压和好的球囊面罩通气，之后才是声门上气道。这和上节课书上的提醒一致：高级气道永远替代不了基础功夫。

slides.q: You and an EMR partner are working an adult cardiac arrest. Compressions and two-person BVM are going well. Per the BC guideline, where does a supraglottic airway fit?
options: Insert it first, before compressions start
A PCP may insert one once high-quality CPR is under way
Pause compressions for 30 seconds to place it
Only after 30 minutes of CPR without ROSC
slides.say: Quick check. You and an EMR partner are working an adult cardiac arrest. Compressions and two-person BVM are going well. According to the BC guideline, where does a supraglottic airway fit? A, insert it first, before compressions start. B, a PCP may insert one once high-quality CPR is under way. C, pause compressions for thirty seconds to place it. D, only after thirty minutes of CPR without ROSC. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 快速检查：你和一位 EMR 搭档在处理一例成人心跳骤停，按压和双人球囊面罩通气都做得很好。按照 BC 指南，声门上气道应该放在什么位置？A 先插，在开始按压之前；B 高质量 CPR 开始之后，PCP 可以置入；C 暂停按压三十秒来放置；D 只有在 CPR 三十分钟仍未恢复自主循环之后。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The BC CPR basics mention SGA insertion by PCPs once high-quality cardiac arrest management has started. A is wrong, because compressions and basic ventilation come first. C is wrong, because BC keeps any pause in compressions under five seconds. D mixes up a different BC number: thirty minutes is a time point for stopping resuscitation, not an airway rule.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。BC 的 CPR 基本概念提到，在高质量心跳骤停处理开始后，由 PCP 置入声门上气道。A 错，按压和基础通气要先做。C 错，BC 要求任何按压中断都不超过五秒。D 混淆了 BC 的另一个数字：三十分钟是终止复苏的时间点，不是气道规则。

slides.title: Drug-assisted intubation (RSI)
slides.body:
Preoxygenate→Sedative→Paralytic→Tube + confirm
  • Book: critical care paramedics or special transport teams
  • Paralytic stops all breathing within about 1 minute
  • Paralysis is not sleep: sedation must come first
  • Combative? Think brain hypoxia until proven otherwise
slides.say: Rapid-sequence intubation, or RSI, means giving a sedative, then a paralytic drug, and intubating right away. The book restricts it to critical care paramedics or specialized transport teams, and none of these drugs are on the BC EMR or PCP drug list. Still, you need to understand what happens. Within about a minute of the paralytic, every skeletal muscle stops, including the diaphragm. The jaw goes slack, the tongue falls back, and a breathing patient becomes apneic with no airway. A paralytic doesn't touch consciousness, so without sedation the patient would be awake and feel everything. And remember: a combative patient may be hypoxic until proven otherwise.
slides.sayZh: 快速序贯插管（RSI）就是先给镇静药、再给肌松药，然后立即插管。书上说这仅限于重症监护救护员或专业转运团队，而这些药都不在 BC 的 EMR 或 PCP 药物清单上。不过，你得明白会发生什么。给了肌松药约一分钟内，全身骨骼肌都停止工作，包括膈肌；下颌松弛、舌根后坠，一个原本能呼吸的病人变成没有呼吸、也没有通畅气道。肌松药不影响意识，所以不先镇静的话，病人是清醒的、什么都感觉得到。还要记住：病人躁动、有攻击性，在排除之前都要当作缺氧。

slides.title: Your role during RSI
slides.body:
• Monitor: ECG, SpO₂, blood pressure; suction on
  • Breathing well: NRB; breathing poorly: assist with BVM
  • High-flow nasal cannula during the attempt
  • SpO₂ falls or 30 s passes: back to BVM, slowly
  • After: tell your partner if HR or BP climbs

The drugs are your partner's. Oxygen is yours.
slides.say: So what does the PCP do during drug-assisted intubation? Your job is oxygen. Make sure the cardiac monitor and pulse oximeter are on, the blood pressure is checked, and suction is ready. If the patient breathes well, a non-rebreather gives high-flow oxygen; if breathing is poor, assist with the BVM. A high-flow nasal cannula can stay on during the attempt. If the saturation drops or thirty seconds pass, the attempt stops and you ventilate, slowly, one second per breath, just to chest rise. Afterwards, a rising heart rate or blood pressure can mean the sedation is wearing off, so tell your partner.
slides.sayZh: 那么在药物辅助插管时，PCP 做什么？你的工作是氧气。确认心电监护和血氧仪都接好，血压测了，吸引器准备好。病人呼吸好，用非重复呼吸面罩给高流量氧；呼吸差，就用球囊面罩辅助通气。插管时可以留着高流量鼻导管。血氧下降或到了三十秒，就停下尝试，由你通气：慢慢来，每次一秒、看到胸廓起伏就停。插管之后，心率或血压上升可能说明镇静在消退，要告诉搭档。

slides.title: The failed airway
slides.body:
Failed airway: SpO₂ can't be kept up during or after attempts, or 3 failed attempts by an experienced intubator

Can't intubate, CAN ventilateBVM, then a rescue SGAbuys time; not definitive
BVM getting hardtwo people, adjuncts, reposition, suctionfix the basics
Can't intubate, can't oxygenatesurgical airwaylast resort
slides.say: Any intubation can fail, so know the definition. A failed airway means the saturation can't be kept at an acceptable level during or after one or more attempts, or three failed attempts by an experienced intubator, even if the saturation holds. What next? Back to basics. In most patients, a good BVM keeps them oxygenated and buys time for plan B, usually a rescue device such as a King LT, LMA or i-gel. These are temporary, not definitive airways. If bagging gets hard, fix the basics: two people, adjuncts, repositioning and suction. Only when the patient can't be intubated and can't be oxygenated does the team move to a surgical airway.
slides.sayZh: 任何插管都可能失败，所以要知道定义。失败气道是指：在一次或多次尝试期间或之后，血氧维持不在可接受水平；或者有经验的操作者累计三次失败，即使血氧还维持得住。接下来怎么办？回到基础。大多数病人，好的球囊面罩通气就能维持氧合，为 B 计划争取时间，B 计划通常是救援装置，比如 King LT、喉罩或 i-gel。这些都是临时气道，不是确定性气道。如果球囊越来越难捏，就把基础做好：两个人、辅助装置、重新摆位、吸引。只有既插不上管、又无法氧合时，团队才会转向外科气道。

slides.title: Cricothyrotomy: the last resort
slides.body:
Open (surgical)Needle
Toolscalpel + tube ≥ 6.0 mm14–16 G catheter + jet ventilation
Agenot under 8 yearssafer in young children
Catchharder to dooxygenates, but CO₂ builds up
  • Site: cricothyroid membrane, below the thyroid cartilage
  • Only if you can't intubate and can't ventilate
slides.say: A cricothyrotomy opens the airway through the cricothyroid membrane, the soft spot just below the thyroid cartilage, or Adam's apple. It's only for the patient who can't be intubated and can't be ventilated: a foreign body that can't be removed, swelling from epiglottitis, anaphylaxis or airway burns, massive facial trauma, or a mouth that won't open. If BVM works, it's not indicated. The open, or surgical, method uses a scalpel and a tube of at least six millimetres, and isn't used under eight years of age. The needle method uses a fourteen to sixteen gauge catheter with jet ventilation. It gives oxygen, but carbon dioxide builds up fast, so it's only a bridge.
slides.sayZh: 环甲膜切开是经环甲膜打开气道，环甲膜就在甲状软骨（喉结）正下方的软凹处。它只用于既插不上管、又无法通气的病人：取不出的异物、会厌炎、过敏或气道烧伤引起的肿胀、严重面部外伤、或张不开口。球囊面罩能通气就不做。开放式（外科）方法用手术刀和内径至少六毫米的导管，八岁以下不用。针刺法用十四到十六号套管针加喷射通气，能给氧，但二氧化碳很快蓄积，所以只是过渡手段。

slides.q: Your partner's second intubation attempt has failed. The patient is unresponsive with no gag reflex. With two-person BVM and an OPA, SpO₂ is back to 95%. Best next step?
options: Have your partner retry at once, without re-oxygenating
Keep up the BVM; consider a rescue SGA and transport
Stop ventilating to see if the patient breathes alone
slides.say: One more decision. Your partner's second intubation attempt has failed. The patient is unresponsive with no gag reflex. With two-person BVM and an oral airway, the saturation is back to ninety-five percent. What's the best next step? A, perform a cricothyrotomy right away. B, have your partner retry at once, without re-oxygenating. C, keep up the BVM, consider a rescue SGA, and transport. D, stop ventilating to see if the patient breathes alone. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 再来一道决策题：搭档第二次插管失败。病人无反应、没有呕吐反射。用双人球囊面罩加口咽通气道后，血氧回到百分之九十五。下一步最好怎么做？A 立即做环甲膜切开；B 让搭档马上再试，不用重新充氧；C 继续球囊面罩通气，考虑救援用的声门上气道，并转运；D 停止通气，看病人能不能自己呼吸。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is C. This patient can't be intubated but can be ventilated, and the BVM is working, so keep it going and consider a rescue SGA while you move toward hospital. A is wrong: a surgical airway is only for a patient you can't intubate and can't oxygenate. B is wrong: the book says to re-oxygenate for thirty seconds to a minute before any new attempt. D is wrong: this unresponsive patient still needs your ventilations.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 C。这位病人插不上管，但能通气，球囊面罩有效，所以继续通气，考虑使用救援用的声门上气道，同时往医院转运。A 错，外科气道只用于既插不上管、又无法氧合的病人。B 错，书上说每次重新尝试前要再充氧三十秒到一分钟。D 错，这位无反应的病人仍然需要你的通气。

slides.title: Stomas and tracheostomy tubes
slides.body:
• Total laryngectomy: breathes only through the stoma
  • Partial: stoma and mouth/nose both carry air
  • BVM to stoma: infant or child mask; seal mouth and nose
  • Trach tube: BVM attaches to its 15/22 mm adapter
  • Sudden distress: think mucus plug; suction ≤ 10 s, ≤ 12 cm
  • BC: tracheostomy is a CPAP contraindication
slides.say: Some patients breathe through a stoma, an opening in the front of the neck. After a total laryngectomy, the voice box is gone, and the mouth and nose no longer connect to the lungs, so bagging the mouth only fills the stomach. After a partial laryngectomy, air moves through both the stoma and the upper airway. To bag a stoma, no head tilt is needed: use an infant or child mask over it, while a second person seals the mouth and nose. A tracheostomy tube has an adapter, so the BVM attaches directly. Sudden distress usually means a mucus plug: suction gently, ten seconds at most, no deeper than twelve centimetres. And in BC, a tracheostomy rules out CPAP.
slides.sayZh: 有些病人经造口呼吸，也就是颈前的一个开口。全喉切除后，喉没有了，口鼻和肺不再相通，所以对着嘴捏球囊只会把气打进胃里。部分喉切除的病人，造口和上呼吸道都能走气。给造口通气不需要仰头：用婴儿或儿童面罩罩住造口，另一个人封住口鼻。气管切开套管有接头，球囊可以直接接上。突然呼吸困难，多半是痰栓堵塞：轻柔吸引，每次最多十秒，插入不超过十二厘米。在 BC，气管切开是 CPAP 的禁忌证。

slides.title: Dentures and facial trauma
slides.body:
• Dentures that fit well: leave them in (better mask seal)
  • Loose ones: take them out; bridges can have sharp metal
  • Best removed before an advanced airway goes in
  • Facial trauma: suction first, then ventilate
  • Suspect the spine: jaw thrust, head neutral and in line
  • Stridor: think swelling of the larynx
slides.say: Two more special cases. Dentures that fit well should stay in, because they hold the face's shape and give you a better mask seal. Loose dentures can block the airway, so take them out, and be careful with bridges, which often have sharp metal edges. If an advanced airway is coming, dentures are best removed first, because pulling them out later can dislodge the tube. Facial trauma bleeds a lot and swells fast. Suction until the airway is clear, then ventilate; bagging into a mouth full of blood almost guarantees aspiration. Facial injuries also raise suspicion of a spine injury, so use a jaw thrust and keep the head neutral. Listen for stridor, a sign of laryngeal swelling.
slides.sayZh: 再讲两种特殊情况。合适的假牙应该留着，因为它撑住面部形状，面罩更容易密封。松动的假牙可能堵住气道，要取出；牙桥要小心，常带锋利的金属边。如果要上高级气道，最好先取出假牙，因为之后再取可能把导管带出来。面部外伤出血多、肿得快。先吸引到气道干净，再通气；对着满口血捏球囊几乎必然导致误吸。面部受伤也要怀疑脊柱损伤，所以用推举下颌法、保持头部中立。留意喘鸣，那是喉部肿胀的征象。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• Paralyzed = no breathing, and maybe aware if sedation fades
  • SGAs leak: suction ready; watch for vomit in the tube
  • Sudden decline: device out, blocked, pneumothorax, equipment
  • Bagging a neck breather's mouth fills the stomach
  • Combative? Check SpO₂; think hypoxia
slides.say: Here's what's new to watch out for. First, a paralyzed patient can't breathe at all, and if the sedation fades, they may be aware. Speak to them kindly, and report any rise in heart rate or blood pressure. Second, supraglottic airways don't fully stop aspiration, so keep suction ready and watch for vomit in the tube. Third, if a patient with any advanced airway suddenly gets worse, run through four causes: the device has moved or come out, it's blocked with secretions, a pneumothorax, or equipment failure. Fourth, bagging the mouth of a neck breather only fills the stomach. And fifth, a combative patient may simply be hypoxic, so check the saturation first.
slides.sayZh: 下面是你要新注意的事。第一，被肌松的病人完全不能呼吸，如果镇静消退，他可能是有意识的；说话要温和，心率或血压一上升就报告。第二，声门上气道不能完全防止误吸，吸引器要备好，留意管内有没有呕吐物。第三，任何上了高级气道的病人突然恶化，按四个原因排查：装置移位或脱出、被分泌物堵塞、气胸、设备故障。第四，对全喉切除的颈呼吸者捏口鼻，只会把气打进胃里。第五，躁动有攻击性的病人可能只是缺氧，先查血氧。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• The book's airway drugs are not on BC's 18-drug list
  • Not on the list either: benzodiazepines, opioid analgesics, atropine
  • No IO procedure on the exam (IV only); BCEHS PCP IO: hypovolemic arrest 12+ or ACP
  • SGA: mentioned for PCPs once high-quality CPR is under way
  • Cardiac arrest: compression pauses under 5 seconds
  • Tracheostomy is a CPAP contraindication
slides.say: Here's how the book lines up with BC. The book describes many airway drugs: sedatives like midazolam and ketamine, opioids like fentanyl, and paralytics like succinylcholine and rocuronium. None of them are on BC's list of eighteen exam drugs. Benzodiazepines, opioid pain medicines and atropine aren't on that list either, even though the book uses them around intubation. For vascular access, the BC exam guidelines only describe IV access, with no procedure for starting an intraosseous, or IO, line. On a BCEHS call, a PCP places an IO only in a cardiac arrest from fluid loss at twelve or older, or with an ACP directing. The BC guideline mentions SGA insertion by PCPs once high-quality CPR is under way, and compression pauses stay under five seconds. And from the special patients: a tracheostomy is a contraindication to CPAP.
slides.sayZh: 下面对照书和 BC。书里讲了很多气道用药：镇静药如咪达唑仑、氯胺酮，阿片类如芬太尼，肌松药如琥珀胆碱、罗库溴铵。这些都不在 BC 的十八种考纲药物里。苯二氮卓类、阿片类镇痛药和阿托品也都不在这份清单上，尽管书上在插管时会用到它们。血管通路方面，BC 考纲只描述了静脉通路，没有建立骨髓腔（IO）通路的操作流程。在 BCEHS 出车中，PCP 只有在十二岁及以上、因失液导致的心脏骤停时，或在 ACP 指挥下，才能建立 IO。BC 指南提到，高质量 CPR 开始后由 PCP 置入声门上气道，按压中断不超过五秒。特殊病人方面：气管切开是 CPAP 的禁忌证。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. SGAs: blind, no gag reflex, not full aspiration protection
  2. RSI and surgical airways are your partner's; oxygen is yours
  3. Failed airway: back to the BVM; surgical airway is last

Next: Chapter 14, mechanical ventilation
slides.say: Three things to remember. One: supraglottic airways go in blind, only in patients with no gag reflex, and they don't fully protect against aspiration. The BC guideline mentions PCPs inserting one in cardiac arrest, once high-quality CPR is under way. Two: drug-assisted intubation and surgical airways belong to your advanced partner, but oxygen is your job from start to finish. Three: when intubation fails, go back to the BVM; a surgical airway is only for the patient who can't be intubated and can't be oxygenated. That completes Chapter thirteen. Next chapter: mechanical ventilation. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，声门上气道是盲插的，只用于没有呕吐反射的病人，也不能完全防止误吸；BC 指南提到，心跳骤停时在高质量 CPR 开始后由 PCP 置入。二，药物辅助插管和外科气道属于你的高级搭档，但从头到尾，氧气都是你的工作。三，插管失败就回到球囊面罩；外科气道只用于既插不上管、又无法氧合的病人。第十三章到此结束。下一章：机械通气。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
